skill.name: Work out a word's meaning from the words around it
skill.why: When you meet a tricky word, the words around it often explain it.
skill.how: Read the sentence and the next one. Find the clues, guess, then test your guess.

steps.say: Stuck on a tricky word? Look at its neighbours.

That's the tricky word itself. Look at its neighbours.

steps.win: Yes! The words around a word are its context.

steps.say: Careful! Some guesses fit the sentence, but not the clue.

Nothing here is about speed. What did Jai do?

steps.win: Yes! Tired fits after footy, but four pies means hungry.

steps.say: Now I test it. I swap my meaning in.

check.nudge: Read it aloud. Would a really hungry person eat four pies?

steps.win: Yes! It makes sense. Ravenous means really hungry.

steps.say: Watch for but. The next part goes the opposite way.

show.nudge: That tells you about Gus. Find the little word that flips things.
Serene is the tricky word. Find the little word before it.

steps.ask: Tap the word that tells you to flip the meaning.
steps.win: Yes! But is an opposite clue. So is on the other hand.

options.reason: But flips it. Wren is the opposite of shaky Gus.
Nothing here is about noise. What's the opposite of shaking with nerves?

steps.win: Yes! Calm, the opposite of nervous. Sipping tea fits too.

steps.say: Some words have more than one meaning. Clues show which.

options.reason: That is another meaning. Can a car spray water at Mo? Find the clue.

steps.win: Yes! A long nose. Elephant and sprayed water are the clues.

terms.means: Words nearby that show what the tricky word means. Often the next sentence.
But, or on the other hand. The word means the opposite of what came before.
Your guess. Swap it in. Still makes sense? You cracked it.

card.test: Find the clue nearby. Guess. Swap your guess in. Does it still make sense?

weDo.hint: What did Gus do with his nose?
weDo.success: Rotten and stinky. Gus held his nose and gagged, so the bin must smell awful.

options.reason: A brand-new bin wouldn't make Gus hold his nose and gag.
Bins can be sticky, but Gus held his nose. Which sense is that a clue about?

weDo.hint: What happened to Zed at the end?
weDo.success: Very sleepy. Zed fell asleep, so drowsy must mean sleepy.

options.reason: Angry people don't fall asleep on their controller. The clue is that he fell asleep.
Nothing in the sentence is about speed. What happened to Zed at the end?

encounters.frame: Mo's cooking diary has a word the Tintacle doesn't know.
encounters.text: Day 12. Today I made toast for the crew. I wanted it golden and crunchy. Then Tully started telling me about the Reef Rays. I forgot all about the toast. Smoke filled the galley and the alarm went off. The toast was scorched. It was black on both sides and as hard as a roof tile. Gus ate his anyway. He said it tasted like a campfire. Wren fed hers to a seagull. The seagull spat it out.
encounters.prompt: What does scorched mean?
encounters.success: Burnt black. The smoke, the alarm and the black sides all tell you the toast burnt.

options.reason: Golden is what Mo wanted. Then came smoke, the alarm and black sides.
The toast was as hard as a roof tile. Does that sound soggy?

encounters.frame: Wren is writing up a rescue in her notebook.
encounters.text: We found a tiny possum under the deck today. It was very timid. When I reached out, it curled into a ball. When Zed sneezed, it ran behind a pot plant and shook. It would not come out for an hour. In the end, I left some apple by the pot. Then I hid behind the door. Only then did the possum creep out to eat.
encounters.prompt: What does timid mean?
encounters.success: Shy and easily scared. It curled up, hid and shook, and only came out when nobody was watching.

options.reason: A fierce possum would fight. This one curled up and hid.
A weak possum couldn't dash behind a pot so fast. Why did it wait until nobody was watching?

encounters.frame: Gus left his lab report open. The Tintacle has turned a worried green.
encounters.text: Experiment 47: The Sock Jar. I sealed one of Mo's footy socks in a jar for three weeks. On day one, it smelled a bit like cheese. By day ten, a grey fuzz had grown over the heel. On day twenty-one, I opened the lid. The smell was so pungent that it made my eyes water from across the room. Wren ran outside gasping for air. The Tintacle turned a sickly green and hid under the bench. Even with every window open, the lab stank for two whole days. Result: never open the jar again. Mo has asked for his sock back. The answer is no.
encounters.prompt: What does pungent mean?
encounters.success: Strong and sharp. The smell made eyes water from across the room and the lab stank for days.

options.reason: That was only day one. What did the smell do on day twenty-one?
Gus never tastes it. His eyes water from across the room, so think about smell.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing tips for his speedrun stream.
encounters.text: Level 9 of Lava Tower is the hardest part of my speedrun. The fireballs are relentless. They keep pouring down the whole time, with no break at all. As soon as you dodge one, three more come flying at you. Most players try to wait for a gap, but there is no gap. I learned to keep running and jump every two beats of the music. My best time is four minutes and twelve seconds. My thumbs were sore for a whole day afterwards. Next week I'm going to try it with my eyes shut. Mo says that is a terrible idea, and that I'll just fall in the lava a lot.
encounters.prompt: What does relentless mean?
encounters.success: Never stopping. The fireballs keep pouring down with no break, and there is no gap.

options.reason: Fast or slow, the next sentence tells you something else about them. Read it again.

encounters.frame: Tully is reading her match report out loud. Twice.
encounters.text: Herons Win the Netball Grand Final! With five seconds left, the scores were level. Then Kira Bell caught a pass right under the ring. She leapt and shot, and the ball dropped through without touching the sides. The buzzer went, and the Herons had won by one goal! The crowd was jubilant. Fans hugged total strangers. Some cried happy tears, and one man threw his hat so high that it landed on the scoreboard. Down on the court, the Herons players hugged each other in a big, sweaty pile. They sang the club song three times. Even the coach, who never smiles, did a little dance beside the bench.

options.reason: The crowd might have been tense before the shot. After the buzzer, they hugged and cried happy tears.

encounters.frame: Wren's diary, written the morning after a bat count.
encounters.text: Last night I went to count the bats in the old mine. Everything about it was eerie. The wind made a low moaning sound through the tunnels. Water dripped somewhere in the dark, but I couldn't see where. My torch flickered. The hairs on my arms stood up, and I kept feeling that someone was standing right behind me. When I turned around, nobody was there. I counted the bats as fast as I could. Then I ran all the way back to the boat without looking behind me. This morning Gus asked if I wanted to go back tonight for a second count. I said no thanks.
encounters.prompt: What does eerie mean?
encounters.success: Strange and creepy. The moaning wind, the hairs standing up and feeling watched are all creepy clues.

options.reason: It was dark, but why did her hairs stand up? Why did she feel watched?
There were sounds, but why did she keep feeling someone was right behind her?

encounters.frame: Indi's sketchbook has a before-and-after page about her new mural.
encounters.text: Before: The wall behind the island shop used to be the dullest thing I had ever seen. It was the grey of old porridge, and the paint was peeling off in sad little curls. I added orange fish with lime-green stripes. Now the wall is so vibrant that people walking past stop in their tracks. A kid on a scooter crashed into a bin because he was staring at it. (He was fine.) The shop owner says her sales have doubled. The Tintacle sat in front of it for an hour, flashing every colour it could, trying to keep up. encounters.frame: Wren's rescue log. The Tintacle is still flashing duck-yellow.
encounters.text: Rescue Log, Thursday. At 4 pm we got a call about a mother duck in the island car park. Her six ducklings had tumbled through a drain grate, and she couldn't reach them. When we arrived, she was frantic. She was racing back and forth across the grate, quacking at the top of her voice and flapping so hard that feathers flew everywhere. She didn't even notice the cars beeping at her. Her ducklings were peeping from the dark water below, and that only made her worse. Gus lifted the grate with a crowbar, and I lay on my stomach and scooped the ducklings out one by one with a fishing net. They were wet and cheeping, but nobody was hurt. The moment the last one was out, the mother duck went completely quiet. She tucked them under her wings and sat down as if nothing had happened. Mo says she looked a bit smug.
encounters.prompt: What does frantic mean?
encounters.success: Wild with worry. Her ducklings were trapped, so she raced about, quacked and flapped until they were safe.

options.reason: She was loud, but she was also racing and flapping. What were all of them about?
She was like this before the crew did anything. Her trapped ducklings were the cause.
She didn't even notice the cars beeping at her. What was she racing over?

encounters.frame: A crackly message reaches the boat from a very lonely rover.
encounters.text: Day 400 on Planet Kreeb. This is Rover Pip, reporting to Earth. In every direction there is nothing but red dust and grey rock. There are no trees, no rivers and no animals. I have not seen a single living thing since I landed. My cameras still work perfectly, but there is nothing to film. I have counted every rock within a kilometre. There are 9,412, and none of them can talk. The wind blows all day, but there is nobody to hear it except me. At night the only light comes from two tiny moons, and it drops to ninety degrees below zero. This is the most desolate place I have ever explored. Yesterday I found a rock shaped like a sandwich and got very excited. It was just a rock. Sometimes I play my landing song just to hear a sound that isn't wind. Please send a friend, even a small one, even a toaster.
encounters.prompt: What does desolate mean?
encounters.success: Empty and lonely. There's nothing alive, nobody to hear the wind, and Pip begs for a friend.

options.reason: It is quiet, but is Pip enjoying it? Look at what Pip begs for at the end.
There's only red dust, grey rock and the light of two tiny moons.
Nothing attacks or threatens Pip. Look at what Pip keeps saying there is none of.

encounters.frame: Mo wrote about the island busking contest for the crew newsletter.
encounters.text: The Hollowgum Busking Contest had been noisy all day. Kids shouted, a dog barked at a drummer, and somebody's ukulele was badly out of tune. A juggler dropped three of his fish, and a seagull stole one. Then an old woman sat down on an upturned bucket and began to play a silver flute. Her music was soft and slow, like water running over stones. Within seconds, the whole crowd was mesmerised. Nobody talked. Nobody checked their phone. A boy holding an ice cream didn't notice it melting down his arm. Even the barking dog lay down and stared at her with its head on one side. When the last note faded, there was a long silence before anyone remembered to clap. She won first prize, a bucket of prawns, and played one more tune for free. This time the dog howled along. The juggler has asked her for flute lessons.
encounters.prompt: What does mesmerised mean?
encounters.success: So fascinated they couldn't look away. Nobody talked, the boy forgot his ice cream and even the dog stared.

options.text: so fascinated they couldn't look away
bored and wanting to go home early
options.reason: Bored people chat and check their phones. Here nobody did, and the boy forgot his ice cream.
The music was soft, but nobody dozed off. Even the dog lay down and stared at her.
They did go quiet, but polite doesn't explain the boy forgetting his melting ice cream.

encounters.frame: Zed's diary, written by torchlight in the back of the boat.
encounters.text: Night three on Hollowgum Island. We had planned to camp at the old quarry, but from the moment we arrived, everything felt ominous. A thick fog rolled in off the water and swallowed the path behind us. The birds, which had been squawking all afternoon, suddenly went completely silent, as if someone had switched them off. Even the frogs had stopped croaking. My torch started to flicker. Far below in the quarry, something was clanking slowly, like a chain being dragged over rock. Gus said it was probably old machinery moving in the wind, but there wasn't any wind. Then the Tintacle, which never stops flashing colours, turned a flat, dull black and squeezed itself into the bottom of my backpack. Wren whispered that animals can often sense trouble coming before people do. That was when we found the sign. Someone had scratched out the words 'Quarry Closed' and written underneath, in fresh red paint, 'Turn back while you can.' We didn't argue. We packed up the tents in about four minutes, which Tully says is a crew record, and we didn't stop running until we could see the lights of the boat. None of us said a word on the way back. Mo claims he wasn't scared, but he slept with the torch on.
encounters.prompt: Zed could have written 'everything felt strange'. What does 'ominous' tell you that 'strange' doesn't?
encounters.success: Ominous points ahead: something bad is coming. Wren's whisper and the 'Turn back' sign carry that warning.

options.reason: Strange would tell you that already. What do Wren's whisper and the sign add?

options.reason: Nothing bad has happened yet. Wren whispers that animals can sense trouble coming.

options.text: that something bad was about to happen to them
that the crew were brave enough to stay the night
options.reason: They packed up in four minutes and ran for the boat. Does that sound like staying?

encounters.frame: Tully's report on the under-12 soccer final. She's still shouting about it.
encounters.text: It all came down to the final penalty. If Harbour Heights scored, they would win the cup, but if our goalkeeper, Sami, saved it, the match would go to sudden death. Every single person in the stands was on their feet, chewing their nails or hiding their eyes behind their hands. Sami, on the other hand, looked completely nonchalant. While the striker placed the ball on the spot, Sami leaned against the goalpost, yawned and retied a bootlace as if he were waiting for a bus. He even waved to his nan in the crowd. His nan, who was the only calm person in the stands apart from Sami, waved back. Our coach was turning purple on the sideline, shouting at him to concentrate. The striker took a long run-up and blasted the ball towards the top corner. Sami simply stepped to his left and caught it against his chest. The crowd went wild, and the Harbour Heights striker sank to the grass with her hands over her face. Sami just shrugged, rolled the ball to the referee and wandered back to his line. Afterwards, a reporter asked him how he had stayed so relaxed. Sami said, 'It's only a game. Is there any orange cake left?'
encounters.prompt: Tully says Sami looked nonchalant. Which meaning fits every clue, right to the end?
encounters.success: Not bothered at all, inside or out. His answer to the reporter shows he wasn't hiding any worry.

options.text: calm outside, but secretly very worried
options.reason: Looked could hint at hiding worry. But what does Sami say to the reporter afterwards?

options.text: truly calm and not bothered at all, inside and out
too lazy to bother trying to save the goal
options.reason: He stepped left and caught a ball blasted at the top corner. Was he not trying?

options.text: worn out and sleepy after a long, hard match
options.reason: He yawned, but he moved fast to make the save. Swap it in: does sleepy fit the catch?

encounters.frame: Gus's lab notebook. The cover says 'Warning: contains worms'.
encounters.text: Experiment 83: How fast do food scraps decompose in a worm farm? On Monday I tipped a bucket of scraps into the crew's worm farm: banana skins, apple cores, carrot tops and one of Mo's burnt pancakes. By Wednesday, the banana skins had turned black and slimy, and they were crawling with worms. The apple cores were soft and brown, and they smelled like old vinegar. A thin white fuzz covered the carrot tops, which Wren says is a kind of mould. By Friday, most of the scraps had fallen apart completely. Where they had been, there was a layer of dark, crumbly stuff that smelled like a forest floor after rain. Wren says gardeners call it the best soil money can't buy, and she has already taken a scoop for her tomatoes. The worms did most of the work, with help from the mould. Only Mo's pancake looked exactly the same as it had on Monday. The worms had crawled straight around it. Conclusion: most food scraps decompose in under a week. Mo's pancakes do not decompose at all, and I am starting to think they might be made of plastic. Next experiment: what is actually in Mo's pancakes?
encounters.prompt: What does decompose mean? Make sure your meaning fits every clue, right up to Friday.
encounters.success: Rot and break down into soil. By Friday the scraps had fallen apart into dark, crumbly soil.

options.text: get eaten by worms until nothing is left
options.reason: Something is left: a layer of dark, crumbly soil. And the mould helped too.

options.text: grow a coat of white fuzz
options.reason: Only the carrot tops grew fuzz, and only by Wednesday. What were the scraps by Friday?

options.text: rot and break down into soil

options.reason: They did that by Wednesday. Read on to Friday. What had they turned into?

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is live-streaming again. The crew is watching on Zed's tablet.
encounters.text: 'Hey, Vantafam! Maxx here, coming to you live from Hollowgum Island, where I have just personally rescued forty-seven rare Creatures with my bare hands!' Maxx held up an empty cage and grinned at the camera. 'They were so grateful that they all flew off to freedom, which is why you can't see any of them right now. Smash that like button!' Behind him, something in the bushes squeaked, and a small furry paw poked out of a sack before Maxx quickly nudged the sack out of shot with his foot. On the boat, the crew were dubious. Gus raised one eyebrow so high it nearly left his face. Tully pointed out that catching forty-seven Creatures would take about a week, and Maxx had only arrived on the island that morning. Wren noticed that the cage still had a price sticker on it. Indi paused the stream and zoomed in on Maxx's boots, which were spotless, even though he claimed to have spent hours wading through mud. Mo pointed out that Maxx's hands, which had supposedly caught forty-seven Creatures, didn't have a single scratch. 'So,' said Mo slowly, 'we don't believe him, right?' Nobody even bothered to answer. Zed was already scrolling through the comments, looking for anyone else who had spotted the sticker.
encounters.prompt: The writer never explains what dubious means. How can you still work it out?
encounters.success: Each crew member finds a reason not to believe Maxx. Put together, dubious means doubtful that it's true.

encounters.frame: The island newspaper reviewed the school concert. The Tintacle went striped with shock.
encounters.prompt: Cacophony could mean 'a very loud noise' or 'a jumble of clashing sounds'. Tap the clue that shows it's a jumble.
encounters.success: Drums out of time with everyone else means the sounds clash. Loud alone could still sound like music.

parts: Review: The Hollowgum Primary Band Concert. I have been to many school concerts, but nothing could have prepared me for Thursday night.

parts.tap: The school hall was packed to the doors.
parts.reason: A packed hall tells you about the crowd, not about the sound.

parts: The Year 5 band had only been practising for two weeks, and it showed. When the conductor raised her stick, forty children started playing, and the result was a cacophony. Trumpets honked,

parts.tap: the drums thumped out of time with everyone else

parts: , and a recorder squealed like a stepped-on cat.

parts.tap: Several parents in the front row quietly put their fingers in their ears.
parts.reason: Fingers in ears fit any very loud noise. Find a clue that the sounds did not fit together.
A toddler might cry at any big noise. Which clue shows the sounds clashed?

parts: The school principal, who was sitting right next to me, looked as if she were trying very hard to smile. Then, halfway through the second song, something unexpected happened. Ella, the smallest player, who had only been given the triangle, began to tap a slow, steady beat. One by one, the other players started to follow her. By the final song, the band sounded almost like music. The audience clapped for five whole minutes, and Ella got the loudest cheer of the night. I would happily go again next year, although I might bring some earplugs.

encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to what spawn means in it. Swap each meaning in to test it.
encounters.success: Ask what spawns, and where. Game sharks appear, real frogs lay eggs, and a hit can lead to new things.

items.text: In the game Reef Quest, a hungry shark spawns every time you open a treasure chest.
items.reason: A shark, but in Reef Quest. Is it laying eggs, or turning up when you open a chest?

items.text: When your character runs out of health, you spawn again at the last checkpoint.
items.reason: Where does your character turn up after running out of health?

items.text: On level six, a fresh wave of zombies spawns near the gate every thirty seconds.
items.reason: What happens near the gate every thirty seconds on level six?

items.text: Every spring, the frogs in the creek leave clumps of spawn stuck to the reeds.
items.reason: What do frogs leave in clumps on reeds in spring?

items.text: Salmon swim hundreds of kilometres upriver to spawn in the stream where they hatched.
items.reason: Why would salmon swim back to the stream where they hatched?

items.text: The surprise hit game spawned a cartoon series, a comic and a range of lunchboxes.
items.reason: A game, but nothing appears inside it. What came after the game was a hit?

items.text: One video of a dancing frog spawned a craze of kids hopping round the playground.
items.reason: A frog, but no eggs. What came after the video?
